Most of us find it hard to believe that the mind is a figment of our imagination.","Rene Descartes said that the only thing he could not doubt was “I think, therefore I am.” Several other psychologists have argued that consciousness exists, but we can ignore it, because it does not help us explain behavior.","However, to call consciousness a fundamental property would mean only that we have given up on explaining it, and it is certainly too soon for that.","One possibility is consciousness evolved as an “add-on” feature of brain functioning that evolved to improve our ability to survive and reproduce. To say that consciousness emerges necessarily from brain activity means that the universe is set up in such a way that certain types of neuronal activity automatically become conscious.","According to the identity position, consciousness does not explain any behavior that brain activity does not explain, because consciousness is the same thing as brain activity.","As one article insightfully pointed out, brain mapping tells us why lemon smells similar to orange, but not why lemon smells like lemon.","The best we can do is answer questions like what brain activity is necessary for consciousness.","Because that internal experience is unobservable, researchers rely on this operational definition: Someone who reports awareness of one stimulus and not another was conscious of the first and not the second. It just means that we seldom use them in research on consciousness, and if we do, we need to find a way for them to indicate awareness or unawareness of a stimulus.","Through most of the twentieth century, psychological researchers avoided the topic of consciousness altogether.","Modern methods have made consciousness research respectable because researchers can record brain activity while using procedures that permit or prevent conscious perception of a stimulus. The strong response to the flashing dots decreases awareness of the steady dot, as well as the brain’s response to it.","Many studies use masking: A brief visual stimulus is preceded, followed, or both by longer interfering stimuli.","Stanislas Dehaene and colleagues flashed a word on a screen for just 29 milliseconds (ms).","On other trials, the researchers flashed a word for the same 29 ms but preceded and followed it with masking patterns: Using fMRI and evoked potentials, the researchers found that the stimulus initially activated the primary visual cortex in both the conscious and unconscious conditions.","In the unconscious condition (masking), the stimulus spread only weakly to areas beyond the primary visual cortex, and nothing reflected it back to magnify the initial response.","Overall, the data imply that consciousness of a stimulus depends on the amount and spread of brain activity. Becoming conscious of something means that its information takes over more of your brain’s activity, and rebounds to magnify the initial activity.","Seeing something requires perceiving where it is, and the red vertical stripes cannot be in the same place as the green horizontal stripes.","Because your brain cannot perceive both patterns in the same location, your perception alternates between the two.","For most people, each perception lasts about 2 to 5 seconds before the other replaces it, although some people switch faster or slower.","These shifts, demonstrating binocular rivalry, are gradual, sweeping from one side to another. Instead of lines, the stimuli could be other images, such as a house versus a face.","Also, an emotionally charged image, such as a face with an emotional expression, holds attention longer than a neutral image.","To make the brain responses easier to distinguish, researchers presented to one eye a stationary stimulus and to the other eye a pattern that pulsated several times per second in size and brightness. When people reported consciousness of the stationary stimulus, the pulsating brain activity was weak.","A related study found that when someone switched between one perception and the other, the brain response changed first in the occipital cortex, and then spread to the other areas.","During binocular rivalry, while you are attending to the stimulus in one eye, your brain does not completely discard information from the other eye.","If it is a word from your own language, it captures your attention faster than a word from a language you do not understand. of faces and other social stimuli than nonsocial stimuli, and more rapidly become aware of a signal previously associated with danger than a safe stimulus.","Given that you become aware of a highly meaningful item faster than something less meaningful, evidently your brain must have decided that the stimulus was meaningful before you became conscious of it!","Consciousness is associated with vigorous activity in the cerebral cortex.","People who have had surgical removal of the cerebellum experience no loss of consciousness, even though the cerebellum has far more neurons and synapses than the cortex.","Evidently consciousness does not depend on the total number of neurons. During an epileptic seizure, neuronal activity is high, but it lacks informative patterns, and consciousness ceases.","Marcello Massimini and Giulio Tononi explored the key differences between conscious and unconscious activity.","If your brain had no task other than detecting the presence of light, or detecting sound waves, consciousness would be irrelevant. The cerebral cortex, unlike the cerebellum, has long-range reciprocal connections enabling each area to influence many others and receive feedback from the others.","Consider the phi phenomenon that perceptual researchers noted long ago: In the simplest case, you see a dot alternating between one position and another, side by side.","It appears to move between the two positions, even though you never see it in the space between them.","When you saw it in the first position, you didn’t know it was going to appear in the second position.","Evidently, you perceived it as moving from one position to the second after it appeared in the second position! Brain activity during decision-making reveals contributions from different areas, including systems involved in learned preferences and changing values."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module introduces biological influences on attachment and social interaction. Compare factual decisions, value decisions, and social responses without assuming the same mechanism explains all three."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m13-3-study-1","text":"Evidence-based decisions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Deciding often involves collecting information and selecting an action when evidence becomes sufficient. Perceptual decision experiments investigate how neural populations represent possible choices and changes in confidence or accumulated evidence. These tasks help link neuronal activity to measurable responses. An observed buildup of activity can be consistent with a decision process, though researchers must consider alternative interpretations involving movement preparation or attention."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m13-3-study-2","text":"Value decisions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Choices involving rewards and costs recruit mechanisms that assess expected outcomes and compare options. Decisions about value are not simply the same as deciding which visual stimulus is present. Motivation, learning, context, and prior experience influence the comparison. A neural response related to reward does not imply a single 'pleasure center' that determines every choice. Multiple systems contribute to selecting what to pursue and how strongly to pursue it."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m13-3-study-3","text":"Individual differences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People vary in impulsivity, preferences, sensitivity to reward, and reactions to uncertainty. Biological research looks for patterns in neural and behavioral measures, but group averages rarely predict one person's choices perfectly. The same individual may behave differently across social circumstances and tasks. A model of decision-making needs to explain both regularities and flexibility."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m13-3-study-4","text":"Love and social neuroscience"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Social interactions involve recognition, emotion, motivation, learning, and bodily states. Research into bonding and love considers hormonal and brain mechanisms, yet social relationships cannot be reduced to a single transmitter or brain area. The module illustrates a broad theme of biological psychology: complex behavior is possible because many specialized processes cooperate. In revision, connect evidence accumulation, expected value, and social motivations while keeping their research questions distinct."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m13-3-h01","text":"Decisions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To answer such questions, you weigh the evidence.","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers almost always simplify the situation to a single choice between just two options .","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m13-3-h02","text":"Factual Decisions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When you make a decision about factual matters, one set of cells accumulates evidence in favor of one choice, another set accumulates evidence for another choice, and a third set compares the two.","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In one study, a rat had to put its nose into a central port, listen to clicks, and then turn to the side with more clicks.","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One set of cells in the posterior parietal cortex responded in proportion to the clicks on the left, and another set responded in proportion to the clicks on the right.","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Whereas cells in the posterior parietal cortex responded in proportion to the number of clicks, responses in the frontal cortex produced an all-or-none outcome, like a scorekeeper who announces which team won the game, regardless of whether the score was close or lopsided.","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Other studies confirmed that certain neurons in the prefrontal cortex, specifically the dorsolateral part of the prefrontal cortex, act as the “scorekeeper” .","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The task is more difficult than it sounds, because only a few dots were moving, and a larger number of dots were appearing and then disappearing at random positions on the screen.","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m13-3-h03","text":"Value Decisions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The animal has to learn probabilistically over many trials, relying mainly on cells in the basal ganglia.","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If the basal ganglia gradually learned that choice A is usually better than B, but something now favors choice B, the rapid-learning prefrontal cortex can overrule the slower-learning basal ganglia .","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people with damage to the prefrontal cortex tend to bet about the same amount each time, based on their average expectation .","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Their basal ganglia learn what usually happens, and they fail to update based on current information.","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The orbitofrontal cortex (Figure 13.17) has multiple functions in decision making that are not easy to summarize.","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In a similar study, if a monkey had a choice between rewards of almost equal value, its orbitofrontal neurons flipped back and forth between two patterns of activity, apparently because the monkey having trouble deciding .","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Impairment or relative inactivity in the orbitofrontal cortex in humans is often associated with poor or impulsive decisions.","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In the experiment, however, people had to discover the payoffs by trial and error.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, if they started with a streak of wins from A and B, they were slow to switch .","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m13-3-h04","text":"Individual Differences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some people make better decisions than others, and everyone makes better decisions at some times than others.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"There can be any number of reasons, but they include some that we might not immediately think of.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with greater heart rate variability from moment to moment tend to make better decisions, especially in situations of risk and uncertainty such as the Iowa Gambling Task .","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The explanation is not known, but one possibility is that changes in vagus factor for cognitive decline in old age .","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People have a great variety of bacteria substances.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, some types of intestinal bacteria produce inflammation, study.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The point is that what we call love combines motivations, emotions, vasopressin has attracted much attention.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Oxytocin stimulates contractions of the uterus during childbirth, stimulates breasts to produce milk, and promotes maternal behavior, social approach, and pair bonding in many mammalian species .","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A common way to study oxytocin’s effects has been to give it as a nasal spray and compare its effects to a placebo.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"These studies imply that oxytocin increases attention to social cues and intensifies existing relationships.","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Furthermore, most studies have used only small numbers of participants, and several results have been difficult to replicate .","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The hypothesis that oxytocin enhances social attention and loving relationships may well be true, but the evidence so far is not convincing.","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m13-3-h06","text":"Social different monkeys, depending on how they had acted in the past.","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Disrupting those neurons left the monkeys responding unselectively, treating equally those that had or had not been helpful in the past .","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Neurons in the hippocampus and amygdala are also necessary for recognizing other .","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some people express more empathy than others do, largely because of culture and .","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, people with frontotemporal dementia seem quite calm, even if their keep track of the score, and it decided based on the last clicks it heard.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":453,"sourcePdfPage":471},{"type":"bullet","text":"The monkey watched for a while, and then had to wait a few seconds before responding.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h02","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472},{"type":"bullet","text":"Within the parietal cortex, one set of cells responded whenever most of the dots moved left, and a different set responded when the dots moved but a risky choice sometimes yields a huge reward and usually yields little, nothing, or even a penalty.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472},{"type":"bullet","text":"Getting a B+ on your term paper might be delightful or disappointing, depending on what you had been expecting.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472},{"type":"bullet","text":"In one study, monkeys could choose between two juices by moving their eyes left or right.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":454,"sourcePdfPage":472},{"type":"bullet","text":"They can always win $100 in play money by playing from decks A or B, or $50 from C or D.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473},{"type":"bullet","text":"Ordinarily, as they sampled from all four decks, they gradually started exhibiting signs of tension whenever they drew a card from A or B, and they shifted their preference toward C and D.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h03","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473},{"type":"bullet","text":"Here is another influence on decision making that we might not think of: The bacteria in the digestive system.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473},{"type":"bullet","text":"When people say they made a bad decision based on a “gut feeling,” it might be literally true.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h04","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473},{"type":"bullet","text":"According to studies using fMRI, looking at pictures of the person you love strongly activates the brain areas associated with reward, in ways resembling the effects of addictive drugs.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473},{"type":"bullet","text":"Much research has investigated its possible ability to intensify love relationships.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473},{"type":"bullet","text":"Unfortunately, the evidence is not as strong as we would hope.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":455,"sourcePdfPage":473},{"type":"bullet","text":"The studies have been “under-powered” in the statistical sense—that is, unable to reliably detect an effect of the expected size.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h05","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474},{"type":"bullet","text":"You help people near you who seem to be in trouble, and you might contribute money to help victims of a natural disaster on the other side of the world.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474},{"type":"bullet","text":"Animals other than humans also display concern about others of their species, especially familiar ones.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474},{"type":"bullet","text":"For example, if you watch someone who is feeling socially rejected by others, you will “feel the pain” and your brain will react accordingly, but you react more strongly if that person is one of your relatives or friends.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474},{"type":"bullet","text":"The most profound deficit occurs in a condition called frontotemporal degenerate.","headingId":"bp14-m13-3-h06","sourcePrintedPage":456,"sourcePdfPage":474},{"type":"bullet","text":"When you make a decision about factual matters, one set of cells accumulates evidence in each possible choice relative to the value of other available choices.","printedPage":457,"pdfPage":475},{"text":"People with damage to the prefrontal cortex are slow to switch strategies in situations such as the Iowa Gambling Task.","printedPage":457,"pdfPage":475},{"text":"Passionate love excites the brain in ways that resemble those of addictive drugs.","printedPage":457,"pdfPage":475},{"text":"Many studies have reported that the hormone oxytocin increases attention to social stimuli and intensifies social relationships. However, although that conclusion may be correct, much of the evidence so far has been weak.","printedPage":457,"pdfPage":475},{"text":"Neurons in the prefrontal cortex respond to others’ social behaviors and influence behavior toward others who have or have not been cooperative in the past.","printedPage":457,"pdfPage":475},{"text":"People with frontotemporal dementia have difficulty with understanding others’ emotions, and respond only weakly to others’ distress.","printedPage":457,"pdfPage":475}],"topicNotes":[{"id":"bp14-m13-3-h01","title":"Decisions","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"facts":[{"text":"To answer such choice, another set accumulates evidence for another choice, and a third set compares the two.","printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":14},{"text":"In one study, a rat had to put its nose into a central port, listen to clicks, and then turn to the side with more clicks.","printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":15},{"text":"One set of cells in the posterior parietal cortex responded in proportion to the clicks on the left, and another set responded in proportion to the clicks on the right.","printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":16},{"text":"Whereas cells in the posterior parietal cortex responded in proportion to the number of clicks, responses in the frontal cortex produced an all-or-none outcome, like a scorekeeper who announces which team won the game, regardless of whether the score was close or lopsided.","printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":17},{"text":"Other studies confirmed that certain neurons in the prefrontal cortex, specifically the dorsolateral part of the prefrontal cortex, act as the “scorekeeper” .","printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":18},{"text":"The task is more difficult than it sounds, because only a few dots were moving, and a larger number of dots were appearing and then disappearing at random positions on the screen.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":19},{"text":"One set of cortical cells responded when the left side was ahead, and another set responded when the right side was ahead.","printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":66},{"text":"After damage to the prefrontal cortex, a rat could not keep track of the score, and it decided based on the last clicks it heard.","printedPage":453,"pdfPage":471,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"The monkey watched for a while, and then had to wait a few seconds before responding.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"Within the parietal cortex, one set of cells responded whenever most of the dots moved left, and a different set responded when the dots moved right.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":69}],"originalFacts":6,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[{"term":"Posterior ganglia.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":21},{"text":"If the basal ganglia gradually learned that choice A is usually better than B, but something now favors choice B, the rapid-learning prefrontal cortex can overrule the slower-learning basal ganglia .","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":22},{"text":"Most people with damage to the prefrontal cortex tend to bet about the same amount each time, based on their average expectation .","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":23},{"text":"Their basal ganglia learn what usually happens, and they fail to update based on current information.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":24},{"text":"The orbitofrontal cortex (Figure 13.17) has multiple functions in decision making that are not easy to summarize.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":25},{"text":"In a similar study, if a monkey had a choice between rewards of almost equal value, its orbitofrontal neurons flipped back and forth between two patterns of activity, apparently because the monkey having trouble deciding .","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":26},{"text":"Impairment or relative inactivity in the orbitofrontal cortex in humans is often associated with poor or impulsive decisions.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":27},{"text":"In the experiment, however, people had to discover the payoffs by trial and error.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":28},{"text":"However, if they started with a streak of wins from A and B, they were slow to switch .","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":29},{"text":"When you make a decision based on preferences, you estimate the probable outcome of each choice, and weigh which outcome seems better.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"Suppose one choice always yields a moderate reward, but a risky choice sometimes yields a huge reward and usually yields little, nothing, or even a penalty.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"Getting a B+ on your term paper might be delightful or disappointing, depending on what you had been expecting.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":72},{"text":"In one study, monkeys could choose between two juices by moving their eyes left or right.","printedPage":454,"pdfPage":472,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":73},{"text":"They can always win $100 in play money by playing from decks A or B, or $50 from C or D.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":74},{"text":"Ordinarily, as they sampled from all four decks, they gradually started exhibiting signs of tension whenever they drew a card from A or B, and they shifted their preference toward C and D.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":75}],"originalFacts":9,"additionalFacts":6,"glossary":[{"term":"Orbitofrontal cortex","definition":"brain area that responds to a reward based on how it compares to other likely outcomes","sourcePrintedPage":629,"sourcePdfPage":647},{"term":"Prefrontal cortex","definition":"anterior portion of the frontal lobe, which responds mostly to the sensory stimuli that signal the need for a movement","sourcePrintedPage":630,"sourcePdfPage":648},{"term":"Basal ganglia","definition":"a group of subcortical forebrain structures lateral to the Differences","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m13-3-h01","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"facts":[{"text":"Some people make better decisions than others, and everyone makes better decisions at some times than others.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":31},{"text":"There can be any number of reasons, but they include some that we might not immediately think of.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":32},{"text":"People with greater heart rate variability from moment to moment tend to make better decisions, especially in situations of risk and uncertainty such as the Iowa Gambling Task .","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":33},{"text":"The explanation is not known, but one possibility is that changes in vagus activity indicate increased mental effort.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":34},{"text":"Fluctuating blood pressure is a risk factor for cognitive decline in old age .","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":35},{"text":"People have a great variety of bacteria in the gut, mostly performing important functions such as breaking down proteins so that they can be absorbed, producing shortchain fatty acids, and helping with immunity against harmful substances.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":36},{"text":"However, some types of intestinal bacteria produce inflammation, impair cognition, and increase the risk of psychological and neurological disorders .","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":37},{"text":"Here is another influence on decision making that we might not think of: The bacteria in the digestive system.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":76},{"text":"When people say they made a bad decision based on a “gut feeling,” it might be literally true.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":77}],"originalFacts":7,"additionalFacts":2,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":230,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":189},{"id":"bp14-m13-3-h05","title":"The Biology of Love","level":1,"parentId":null,"printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"facts":[{"text":"Social neuroscience , the study of how genes, chemicals, and brain areas contribute to social behavior, is a relatively new area of study.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":39},{"text":"The point is that what we call love combines motivations, emotions, memories, and cognitions.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":40},{"text":"The role of oxytocin and the closely related hormone vasopressin has attracted much attention.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":41},{"text":"Oxytocin stimulates contractions of the uterus during childbirth, stimulates breasts to produce milk, and promotes maternal behavior, social approach, and pair bonding in many mammalian species .","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":42},{"text":"A common way to study oxytocin’s effects has been to give it as a nasal spray and compare its effects to a placebo.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":43},{"text":"These studies imply that oxytocin increases attention to social cues and intensifies existing relationships.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":44},{"text":"Furthermore, most studies have used only small numbers of participants, and several results have been difficult to replicate .","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":45},{"text":"The hypothesis that oxytocin enhances social attention and loving relationships may well be true, but the evidence so far is not convincing.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":46},{"text":"According to studies using fMRI, looking at pictures of the person you love strongly activates the brain areas associated with reward, in ways resembling the effects of addictive drugs.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"Much research has investigated its possible ability to intensify love relationships.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"Unfortunately, the evidence is not as strong as we would hope.","printedPage":455,"pdfPage":473,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":80},{"text":"The studies have been “under-powered” in the statistical sense—that is, unable to reliably detect an effect of the expected size.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":81}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":4,"glossary":[{"term":"Social another.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"Neurons in the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex responded specifically to different monkeys, depending on how they had acted in the past.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"Disrupting those neurons left the monkeys responding unselectively, treating equally those that had or had not been helpful in the past .","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":50},{"text":"Neurons in the hippocampus and amygdala are also necessary for recognizing other individuals and establishing relationships with them .","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":51},{"text":"In another study of monkeys, fMRI located a network of neurons in the prefrontal cortex that respond strongly to videos of social behaviors of other monkeys.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":52},{"text":"The prefrontal areas important for social behavior may not be devoted exclusively to social stimuli.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":53},{"text":"Researchers found similar results in the fMRI results for people playing a game against another person or playing a similar game against a computer program .","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":54},{"text":"Some people express more empathy than others do, largely because of culture and family upbringing, but also because of biological factors.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":55},{"text":"The damage usually includes the ventromedial prefrontal cortex and orbitofrontal cortex, which are important for evaluating possible rewards and also for interpreting other people’s emotional expressions .","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":56},{"text":"In contrast, people with frontotemporal dementia seem quite calm, even if their singing is dismally bad .","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":57},{"text":"You help people near you who seem to be in trouble, and you might contribute money to help victims of a natural disaster on the other side of the world.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":82},{"text":"Animals other than humans also display concern about others of their species, especially familiar ones.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"For example, if you watch someone who is feeling socially rejected by others, you will “feel the pain” and your brain will react accordingly, but you react more strongly if that person is one of your relatives or friends.","printedPage":456,"pdfPage":474,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":84},{"text":"The most profound deficit occurs in a condition called frontotemporal dementia, in which parts of the frontal and temporal lobes of the cerebral cortex gradually The text examines dopamine, cravings, tolerance, withdrawal, and attempts to reduce stress through drug use."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Genetic and behavioral predispositions affect risk, and treatments differ across substances. Distinguish short-term drug effects from adaptations that contribute to repeated use, and distinguish treatments for alcohol and opioid-related problems."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-1","text":"Substance use and reinforcement"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Psychoactive substances influence brain signaling in different ways, and repeated use can alter motivation and behavior. The reward-related role of dopamine is important but should not be translated into the simplistic claim that dopamine means pleasure or directly causes all addictions. Learning, expectation, environment, and stress influence the likelihood of seeking a substance. A substance-use problem involves persistent harmful patterns, not just the presence of a chemical in the body."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-2","text":"Tolerance, withdrawal, and craving"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Tolerance describes a reduced response to a repeated dose or a need for more of a substance to produce a previous effect. Withdrawal refers to reactions that may occur when use is reduced or stopped after adaptation. Craving is a strong motivation or urge to use. These processes can occur together but are not interchangeable, and not all drugs produce identical patterns. Learned cues can trigger seeking even after acute withdrawal has passed, showing that addiction involves more than physical dependence."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-3","text":"Why risk differs"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Genetic predispositions, environmental exposure, stress, learning history, and the specific pharmacological actions of a drug all contribute to risk. Studies of alcohol and opioid-related problems illustrate both shared and distinct mechanisms. A person's course cannot be predicted from one dopamine measurement or one family-history fact. Distinguish susceptibility from inevitability, and examine why certain settings increase the probability that drug use is repeated."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m14-1-study-4","text":"Treatment principles"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Different treatments aim to reduce harmful use, manage withdrawal, block or substitute some drug effects, and change learned behavioral patterns. Medication and behavioral strategies can complement one another, depending on the substance and circumstances. Successful recovery often requires addressing social and environmental conditions as well as neural adaptation. Because drug problems have multiple influences, no one intervention is appropriate for every person."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h01","text":"Drug Effects"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Nicotine comes from tobacco, caffeine from coffee and tea, opiates from poppies, and cocaine from coca.","sourcePrintedPage":462,"sourcePdfPage":480,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A drug that blocks a neurotransmitter is an antagonist , whereas a drug that mimics or increases the effects is an agonist . (The term agonist is derived from a Greek word meaning “contestant.” The term agony derives from the same root.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An antagonist is an “anti-agonist,” or member of the opposing team.) A mixed agonist–antagonist is an agonist for some effects and an antagonist for others, or an agonist at some doses and an antagonist at others.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Investigators say that a drug has an affinity for a receptor if it binds to it, like a key into a lock.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The effectiveness and side effects of any drug vary from one person to another, because drugs affect several kinds of receptors.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One person might have more dopamine type D 4 receptors and fewer D 1 or D 2 receptors, whereas someone else has the reverse .","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h02","text":"The Role of Dopamine"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"James Olds and Peter Milner wanted to test whether stimulation of a certain brain area might influence which direction a rat turns.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"To their surprise, when the rat received the brain stimulation, it sat up, looked around, and sniffed, as if reacting to a favorable stimulus.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Stimulant drugs such as cocaine and amphetamine increase or prolong the release of dopamine in the nucleus accumbens .","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Nicotine stimulates neurons that release dopamine , and opiates inhibit neurons that inhibit dopamine release.","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"dopamine in the nucleus accumbens , along with music , the taste of sugar , and simply imagining something pleasant .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Although it seems natural to assume from all this that dopamine mediates pleasure, much research makes that idea seem uncertain .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dopamine is important for the motivation to get something (wanting), but not necessarily for enjoying it.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with decreased dopamine, such as Parkinson’s disease patients, can still enjoy a tasty treat, apparently as much as ever.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h03","text":"Cravings"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Seeing a lit cigarette triggers a craving in smokers , a video of cocaine use triggers cravings in cocaine users , and the sight of a videogame triggers craving in an excessive videogame player .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people who become addicted to a substance do not enjoy the experience as much as before, but they continue to want it .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cravings are persistent because of changes in the brain.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As Nora Volkow and others have demonstrated, after people become addicted to a drug, the drug releases less dopamine, but cues associated with the drug release more .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cues for the drug attract even more attention because of the decreased competition .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"These results match indications that craving increases during the early stage of abstinence, and slightly declines later .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Repeated alcohol or cocaine use also decreases blood flow and metabolism in the prefrontal cortex, resulting in decreased ability to restrain impulses .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h04","text":"Tolerance and Withdrawal"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of tolerance, heroin users raise their amount and frequency of use to greater and greater levels, eventually taking amounts that could kill other people.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"For example, rats that consistently receive a drug in a distinctive location show more tolerance there than elsewhere .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Cues associated with receiving the drug activate learned mechanisms that counteract the effects of the drug.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because tolerance is learned, it can be weakened through extinction procedures.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If the rat then receives repeated injections of salt water without morphine, it weakens its learned connection between injection and morphine.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The result is decreased tolerance the next time it receives a morphine injection .","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As the body comes to expect the drug, it reacts strongly when the drug is absent.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The withdrawal symptoms after someone quits heroin or other opiates include anxiety, sweating, vomiting, and diarrhea.","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Efforts to avoid withdrawal symptoms contribute to addictive behaviors, but they are generally a minor contributor.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h05","text":"Drug Use for Stress Reduction"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One reason for an addiction is that a user learns to use the substance (or gambling habit or other addiction) to cope with stress.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers gave rats an opportunity to press a lever to inject themselves with heroin.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Midway through the withdrawal period, some of the rats had an opportunity to self-administer heroin again, while others went through withdrawal without heroin.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Later, when rats went through withdrawal a second time, all the rats had an opportunity to press a lever to try to get heroin, but this time, the lever was inoperative.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evidently, receiving an addictive drug during a withdrawal period is a powerful experience.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h06","text":"Predispositions"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people drink alcohol in moderation, but others develop a habit of abuse.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Even among mice, some develop compulsive alcohol use when given the opportunity, and some do not .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A great deal of the predisposition depends on experience.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People who had abusive experiences in childhood are more vulnerable, as is a child whose mother drank too much alcohol during pregnancy .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Children who grew up without careful parental supervision are more likely to develop impulse problems than children of more attentive parents .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As a rule, people with early-onset alcoholism (before age 25) have a family history of alcoholism, a genetic predisposition, and a rapid onset of the problem.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h07","text":"Genetic Influences"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The probability of abusing alcohol or other drugs also relates to genetic influences.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Parents’ alcohol use correlates more strongly with that of their biological children than their adopted children .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Several genes affect the probability of substance use, with effects that vary from one environment to another .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most of these genes are non-specific, increasing the risk of several mental disorders, and risk-taking behaviors in general .","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One gene with a well-confirmed influence on alcohol abuse controls the metabolism of alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In fact, this is the only case of a common gene with a substantial effect on a human psychological disorder (other than Huntington’s disease).","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with a gene that produces less acetaldehyde dehydrogenase metabolize acetaldehyde more slowly.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If they drink much alcohol, they accumulate acetaldehyde, which produces flushing of the face, increased heart rate, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, impaired breathing, and tissue damage.","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h08","text":"Behavioral Predictors of Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"If genes, early environment, or anything else predisposes certain people to drug or alcohol abuse, presumably the predisposition alters behavioral reactions to the substance.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"By the time someone has developed a serious substance abuse problem, overcoming it is difficult.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Such studies find that alcoholism is more likely among those who were described in childhood as impulsive, risk taking, easily bored, sensation seeking, and outgoing .","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because of the strong familial tendency toward alcoholism, researchers expect that many of the sons of alcoholics are future alcoholics themselves.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most robust finding is that most sons of alcoholics show less than average intoxication after drinking a moderate amount of alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Presumably, someone who starts feeling tipsy after a couple of drinks stops at that point.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Follow-up studies found that men who report low intoxication after moderate drinking are more likely than others to develop an alcohol abuse problem .","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h09","text":"Treatments"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research has revealed much about the mechanisms of addiction.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Unfortunately, our increased understanding has not yet translated into better forms of treatment .","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In fact, that is the case for psychopathology in general.","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Research over recent decades has learned much about the genes, neurotransmitters, and other biological","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"factors related to disorders, but treatment outcomes have not improved noticeably .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most common treatment for substance abuse, especially in the United States, is participation in Alcoholics Anonymous, Narcotics Anonymous, or similar organizations.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A smaller number of people consult a psychotherapist.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Not many people turn to medications, but a few options are available.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h10","text":"Medications to Combat Alcohol Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As mentioned, the liver metabolizes alcohol into acetaldehyde (toxic) and then into acetic acid (harmless).","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The drug disulfiram, which goes by the trade name Antabuse , antagonizes the enzyme that metabolizes acetaldehyde.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Ordinarily, that result would indicate that a drug is ineffective, but Antabuse is a special case because of why it is similar to the placebo.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Antabuse is about equal to placebo not because Antabuse is ineffective, but because thinking that a placebo might be Antabuse makes the placebo effective .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A related idea is to have people drink alcohol and then immediately take a drug that produces nausea, thereby forming a learned aversion to the taste of the alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That procedure usually produces quick and effective avoidance of alcohol, although its use has never been popular .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Other medications are naloxone (trade name Revia) and naltrexone, which block opiate receptors and thereby decrease the pleasure from alcohol.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h11","text":"Medications to Combat Opiate Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some physicians at the time recommended that people using alcohol switch to heroin .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Still, the idea has persisted that people who cannot quit opiates might switch to a less harmful drug.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Methadone (METH-uh-don), similar to heroin and morphine, activates the same brain receptors and produces the same effects, but it has the advantage that it can be taken orally.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Methadone taken orally slowly enters the blood and then the brain, avoiding a “rush” that disrupts behavior.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because methadone leaves the brain slowly, the withdrawal symptoms are also gradual.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Buprenorphine and levomethadyl acetate (LAAM), drugs similar to methadone, are also used to treat opiate addiction.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Anecdotal reports have stated that a drug called ibogaine reduces cravings and decreases the probability of drug relapse.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, ibogaine causes hallucinations, and it can damage the heart.","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"So far, we know that it reduces alcohol and heroin seeking in mice, and we await results from human trials .","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m14-1-h12","text":"In Closing: The Psychology and Biology of Substance Abuse"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many people say that alcoholism or other drug addiction is a disease.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dis-ease is literally lack of ease, so in a sense anything that causes difficulty in life is a disease.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, the term disease is generally taken to imply that the problem calls for medical intervention.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Addiction alters the brain’s reaction to the drug, cues for the drug, and other events.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Addiction is a complex problem that requires attention to both the physiology and the social environment.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They’re also presented in alphabetical order with definitions in the book’s Subject Index/Glossary at the end of this book.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The research on sensitization of the nucleus accumbens dealt with addictive drugs, mainly cocaine.","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Nearly all neurotransmitters and hormones are the same in humans as in other species.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":462,"sourcePdfPage":480},{"type":"bullet","text":"So, if a plant evolves a chemical to attract bees, repel caterpillars, or whatever, that chemical is likely to affect humans also.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":462,"sourcePdfPage":480},{"type":"bullet","text":"A drug’s efficacy is its tendency to activate the receptor.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"A drug that binds to a receptor but fails to stimulate it has affinity but not efficacy.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h01","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"When a pair of young psychologists were trying to answer an unrelated question, their accidental findings led to the discovery of the importance of dopamine in motivation.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"When they implanted their electrode, they missed the intended target and instead hit an area called the septum.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":463,"sourcePdfPage":481},{"type":"bullet","text":"Gambling activates this area for habitual gamblers, and videogame playing activates it for habitual videogame players.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"You might like a fattening dessert without wanting it, and you might want a medicine without liking it.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h02","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even after prolonged abstinence, cues associated with the habit trigger a renewed craving.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even after a long period of abstinence, the cues continue to grab attention and trigger a craving.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"During a period of abstinence, the nucleus accumbens synapses responding to drug cues become even more sensitive for a while, before partly declining later.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h03","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"After many injections of morphine, a rat develops tolerance to it.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Symptoms of alcohol withdrawal include irritability, fatigue, shaking, sweating, and nausea.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":464,"sourcePdfPage":482},{"type":"bullet","text":"Cocaine is addictive even though the withdrawal symptoms are mild.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Gambling can be a powerful addiction, even though no substance is withdrawn.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h04","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Although both groups of rats pressed the lever, those that had self-administered heroin during the previous withdrawal state pressed more frequently.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Users—rat or human—learn that the drug relieves the distress caused by drug withdrawal.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"The users then crave the drug during other kinds of distress.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h05","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"With other substances also, only some of the users develop an addiction.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"People with later onset are more likely to have reacted to life difficulties, less likely to have a family history of alcoholism, and more likely to respond well to treatment.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h06","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"After anyone drinks ethyl alcohol, enzymes in the liver metabolize it to acetaldehyde, a toxic substance.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"More than a third of the people in China and Japan have a gene that slows acetaldehyde metabolism.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"Probably for that reason, alcohol abuse has historically been uncommon in those countries.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h07","sourcePrintedPage":465,"sourcePdfPage":483},{"type":"bullet","text":"If so, it should be possible to monitor behavior of young people and predict their risk for later problems.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"Other research follows this design: First, identify young men who are not yet problem drinkers.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"If someone with strong intoxication from a moderate intake does develop an alcohol problem, it is usually less severe than that of other abusers.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"The advice is, if you “hold your liquor well,” it is not something to brag about, but something to worry about.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h08","sourcePrintedPage":466,"sourcePdfPage":484},{"type":"bullet","text":"Soon therapists tried using disulfiram as a drug, hoping that those with alcoholism would associate alcohol with illness and stop drinking.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"When people take Antabuse, or a placebo that they think might be Antabuse, the threat of becoming ill strongly discourages any attempt to drink alcohol.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h10","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"Heroin is an artificial substance invented in the 1800s as a supposedly safer alternative for people who were trying to quit morphine.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"LAAM has the advantage of producing a longlasting effect so that the person visits a clinic three times a week instead of daily.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h11","sourcePrintedPage":467,"sourcePdfPage":485},{"type":"bullet","text":"Calling addiction a disease helps to reduce some of the guilt and stigma.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486},{"type":"bullet","text":"As you have seen in this module, addiction does have a physiological basis.","headingId":"bp14-m14-1-h12","sourcePrintedPage":468,"sourcePdfPage":486}],"topicIds":["bp14-m14-1-h01","bp14-m14-1-h02","bp14-m14-1-h03","bp14-m14-1-h04","bp14-m14-1-h05","bp14-m14-1-h06","bp14-m14-1-h07","bp14-m14-1-h08","bp14-m14-1-h09","bp14-m14-1-h10","bp14-m14-1-h11","bp14-m14-1-h12"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-1","title":"Substance The reward-related role of dopamine is important but should not be translated into the simplistic claim that dopamine means pleasure or directly causes all addictions. Learning, expectation, environment, and stress influence the likelihood of seeking a substance. A substance-use problem involves persistent harmful patterns, not just the presence of a chemical in the body.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":462,"sourcePrintedEnd":469,"sourcePdfStart":480,"sourcePdfEnd":487},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-2","title":"Tolerance, withdrawal, and craving","text":"Tolerance describes a reduced response to a repeated dose or a need for more of a substance to produce a previous effect. Withdrawal refers to reactions that may occur when use is reduced or stopped after adaptation. Craving is a strong motivation or urge to use. These processes can occur together but are not interchangeable, and not all drugs produce identical patterns. Learned cues can trigger seeking even after acute withdrawal has passed, showing that addiction involves more than physical dependence.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":462,"sourcePrintedEnd":469,"sourcePdfStart":480,"sourcePdfEnd":487},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-3","title":"Why risk differs","text":"Genetic predispositions, environmental exposure, stress, learning history, and the specific pharmacological actions of a drug all contribute to risk. Studies of alcohol and opioid-related problems illustrate both shared and distinct mechanisms. A person's course cannot be predicted from one dopamine measurement or one family-history fact. Distinguish susceptibility from inevitability, and examine why certain settings increase the probability that drug use is repeated.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":462,"sourcePrintedEnd":469,"sourcePdfStart":480,"sourcePdfEnd":487},{"id":"bp14-m14-1-study-4","title":"Treatment principles","text":"Different treatments aim to reduce harmful use, manage withdrawal, block or substitute some drug effects, and change learned behavioral patterns. Medication and behavioral strategies can complement one another, depending on the substance and circumstances. Successful recovery often requires addressing social and environmental conditions as well as neural adaptation.
